solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mariner admitting flagrant loss of trust transformed battle

indicators.note: a loss means something is taken away, so the named letters drop out of the word before them
what is transformed changes its form, so the remaining letters are rearranged
to admit is to let in, so the sailor's word holds the rearranged letters inside it

blocks.note: a tar is a sailor
taken as written
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A sailor betrays a trust in some shocking way and is changed by the experience.
explanation.walkthrough: Trust is the National Trust, the British heritage charity; the sailor's word splits after its first letter to hold the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Trafalgar was the 1805 naval engagement off Spain where Nelson defeated the French and Spanish fleets.

clue.text: Trails of Connexion on TV coming up over weekend

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top
the reversed word sits over and around the end letter, enclosing it

blocks.note: a SCART is the plug-and-socket connector on older televisions
the end of the word week

explanation.surface: Something about the tracks of a TV show called Connexion being broadcast at the weekend.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracks are the marks or paths left behind, so they are trails in the sense of footprints or routes.

clue.text: Serving "Policeman" goes after lassie's heart

indicators.note: a heart is the centre, so only the inner letters of the girl's word are used

blocks.note: the word lassie with its outer letters removed
Sting was the singer of the band The Police, hence the quotation marks

explanation.surface: A police officer follows a girl's heart, a little romance on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes around Policeman hint it is not a real officer but a member of The Police; 'goes after' puts his name after the lassie's centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Serving and assisting both mean helping or waiting on someone, as a server assists diners.

clue.text: "Endeavour" is at provisional start of trip

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is taken

blocks.note: taken as written
a temp is a temporary, provisional worker
first letter of trip

explanation.surface: The TV detective Endeavour is on a temporary first leg of a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes make Endeavour look like the Morse prequel's title; it is simply the noun meaning an effort.
explanation.definitionFit: An endeavour is an effort or try, which is what an attempt is.

clue.text: Fish move past

blocks.note: first meaning: a small spiny-finned fish
second meaning, as two words: to pass something

explanation.walkthrough: Fish looks like a verb here, but it is a noun naming the creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The goby is a small fish of rock pools, and to go by is to pass or move past.

clue.text: Split in lower ranks of Lyceum after official vote

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower ranks are the bottom letters, so the final three are taken
the word for split goes inside the selected letters
this word places the remaining parts after the official's short title

blocks.note: a ref is a referee, a match official
the last three letters of Lyceum
to rend is to split or tear

explanation.surface: A division among junior members of a school or theatre follows an official vote.
explanation.definitionFit: A referendum is a direct popular vote on a single question.

clue.text: Moor as PM

blocks.note: first meaning: open uncultivated land
second meaning: Edward ..., British Prime Minister 1970 to 1974

explanation.walkthrough: Moor could be a verb (to moor a boat); it is the open land.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathland is open moorland, and Edward Heath was a Conservative prime minister of the UK.

clue.text: Listing forwards' duty?

blocks.note: first meaning: a ship leaning over to one side
second meaning: in a rugby scrum the forwards hook the ball back with their feet

explanation.walkthrough: Forwards are rugby players; the question mark flags the playful sense of what they do in the scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship heeling over tilts sideways, and in rugby forwards push the ball back with the heel in the scrum.

clue.text: Port bow rises with changeable current

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the word is turned round

blocks.note: AC is alternating current, which changes direction
a bow is an arc shape

explanation.surface: A ship's port bow lifts in a shifting current, all nautical terms.
explanation.walkthrough: Port and bow both look like sides of a ship; port is the definition and bow is a curve.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital of Ghana and a seaport on the Gulf of Guinea.

clue.text: Allowance in latitude he soon worked out – aboard 18?

indicators.note: worked out means solved or reshaped, so these letters are rearranged
the allowance word sits inside the rearranged letters

blocks.note: a ration is a fixed allowance
L is the abbreviation for latitude
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone works out how much leeway they have, wondering who was aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is VICTORY, Nelson's flagship at Trafalgar; the rearranged letters split around the allowance word.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiral Lord Nelson commanded the fleet from HMS Victory and died aboard her at Trafalgar.

clue.text: Nineties account returned with advantage

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read right to left

blocks.note: a TESSA was a tax-exempt special savings account, a UK product of the 1990s

explanation.surface: A bank account from the 1990s pays out with some benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: A TESSA was a British tax-free savings account available from 1991 to 1999.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is something useful or valuable, a benefit, which is what an advantage is.

clue.text: Coach expert to cater innovatively

indicators.note: doing something innovatively means in a new way, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: a buff is an enthusiast or expert
the word cater, rearranged

explanation.surface: A sports coach expert at catering in fresh ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Coach suggests a trainer, but it is a railway carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffet car is a railway carriage serving food, and coach is another word for a railway carriage.

clue.text: Last request from X tough on setter

indicators.note: in an across clue one part on another follows it, so the tough word comes after the setter

blocks.note: X is the written sign for a kiss
the setter refers to themself as me
hardy means tough and robust

explanation.surface: A condemned person called X makes a tough final request of the setter.
explanation.walkthrough: These were reputedly Nelson's dying words to his flag captain Thomas Hardy aboard Victory.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is famously the final request Nelson made as he lay dying at Trafalgar.

clue.text: Miss Hayworth's aboard faulty train — a damned nuisance…

indicators.note: the dash works as a minus sign, taking the following letter away
something faulty is wrongly put together, so the letters are rearranged
being aboard means being inside a vehicle, so the name goes inside

blocks.note: Rita Hayworth, the Hollywood film star
taken as written
the letter removed from the vehicle word

explanation.surface: A film star is aboard a broken-down train, and that is a real nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash works as a minus sign, a device easy to read past as mere punctuation; the ellipsis carries the sentence on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An irritant is anything that annoys or provokes, a source of persistent bother.

clue.text: Father Mark's unfortunate – Casualty is anodyne

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
ink is what leaves a mark on paper
ill as in ill luck, unlucky
ER is the emergency room, the hospital casualty department

explanation.surface: A priest named Mark has a bad time, and the TV drama Casualty is bland.
explanation.walkthrough: Casualty is the long-running BBC hospital drama, but here it stands for the emergency department; anodyne looks like 'bland' but means pain-relieving.
explanation.definitionFit: An anodyne is a medicine that soothes pain, the older word for a painkilling drug.

clue.text: … Requisition one on the Underground?

blocks.note: first meaning: to seize goods in settlement of a debt
second meaning, playfully split: a train on the District line of the London Underground

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the previous clue's nuisance; read as DIS TRAIN, the word becomes a District line train, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To distrain is the legal act of seizing property to recover a debt, a kind of requisition.

clue.text: Returning fillet of turbot suggests zeal

indicators.note: a fillet is a slice cut from inside, so the letters come from within the words
returning means going back, so the found letters read right to left

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A fish dish sent back to the kitchen shows enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enjoyment and enthusiasm, a close synonym for zeal.

clue.text: Fare from Belgian town slum area reduced on 4th of April?

indicators.note: something reduced is cut down, so the slum word loses its last letter
the fourth of a word is its fourth letter only

blocks.note: Spa is the Belgian resort town that gave its name to all spas
a ghetto is a deprived urban area
the fourth letter of April

explanation.surface: Food from a Belgian slum area, cut-price on the fourth day of April.
explanation.walkthrough: The '4th of April' looks like a date, but it is the fourth letter of the word April.
explanation.definitionFit: Fare means food served, and spaghetti is a staple Italian pasta dish.

clue.text: Origins of geological events seen in Nevada desert region

indicators.note: origins are beginnings, so the opening letters of the following words are used
to be seen in a place is to be inside it

blocks.note: Nev. is the abbreviation for the US state of Nevada
the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: The origins of geological events are seen in the Nevada desert.
explanation.definitionFit: The Negev is the large desert region in southern Israel.

clue.text: Operation on hernia's quite imminent

indicators.note: an operation works on something and alters it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Surgery on a hernia is due soon.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearish means fairly near, so something nearish in time is quite imminent.

clue.text: Endlessly failing Conservative achieves success

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: a vice is a moral failing
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Conservative who keeps failing still somehow wins.
explanation.walkthrough: Failing looks like a verb; it is the noun for a flaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A victory is a win, a triumph, which is a form of success.

clue.text: Like 8 21, and not a soft touch, by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase asks for a word heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: a tickle is a soft touch

explanation.surface: Someone resembling Nelson is no pushover, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 21 is Horatio Nelson; 'soft touch' usually means a pushover, but here it is a gentle tickle.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson was an admiral, so anything like him is seafaring, to do with ships and sailors.

clue.text: Former Caucasian secret policeman held in Indiana

indicators.note: something held in is enclosed, so the policeman's name sits inside the state abbreviation

blocks.note: IN is the postal abbreviation for Indiana
Lavrentiy Beria headed Stalin's secret police

explanation.surface: A former white man who was a secret policeman is detained in Indiana.
explanation.walkthrough: Caucasian suggests a white person, but means from the Caucasus: Iberia was an ancient kingdom in what is now Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caucasian Iberians lived in the ancient Georgian kingdom of Iberia, a people now long gone.

clue.text: See 8
Revolutionary style by an Arabian

indicators.note: placed by means set beside, so the style word follows the others

blocks.note: taken as written
Ar. is an abbreviation for Arabian or Arabic
chic is stylishness

explanation.surface: An Arab dresses in a radical new fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolutionary suggests 'new style', but the definition means lawless.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchic means without order or government, the state a revolutionary seeks to overturn.

clue.text: "Proceed with caution" in child-free room

indicators.note: free of something means without it, so the child abbreviation is removed

blocks.note: ch. is the abbreviation for child
a chamber is a room

explanation.surface: Be careful in a room with no children.
explanation.definitionFit: On traffic lights the yellow signal means prepare to stop, which is a warning to drive with caution.

clue.text: Steer sheep for shearing? that's a giggle!

indicators.note: shearing clips off the edges, so each word loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: steer with its outer letters trimmed
sheep with its outer letters trimmed

explanation.surface: A farmer drives sheep to be sheared, and finds it funny.
explanation.walkthrough: Steer can be a verb or a young bullock; either way, both animals' words get their ends sheared off.
explanation.definitionFit: Tee-hee is the imitative word for a stifled laugh, a little giggle.

clue.text: Colouring Woss's way?

indicators.note: Jonathan Ross is mocked as Woss for saying his R as W, so his version swaps that letter

blocks.note: a road is a way

explanation.surface: Something about the way TV host Jonathan Ross colours things.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan Ross, the British TV presenter, pronounces R as W, so his way is WOAD; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: Woad is a plant yielding a blue dye, famously used by ancient Britons as body colouring.

clue.text: Setter's sibling beginning to get picture over quandary

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter alone
turning a word over flips it so it reads backwards

blocks.note: the setter says I'm, I am
bro is short for brother
first letter of get
an oil is an oil painting

explanation.surface: The setter's brother is starting to take a picture of a tricky situation.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is a confused, embarrassing situation, a tangled predicament or quandary.

clue.text: Jots heading down in strange patois

indicators.note: with its head down and gone, the word loses its first letter
something strange is out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Notes are jotted down in an odd local dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: Jots looks like a verb for writing notes; it is the plural noun meaning tiny amounts.
explanation.definitionFit: An iota and a jot are both a very small amount, from the smallest Greek letter.

clue.text: See 11
New designer employed as standard

indicators.note: letters employed are put to work in a new arrangement rather than left as they stand

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newly hired designer is taken on as the norm.
explanation.walkthrough: New looks like the anagram signal but is just its abbreviation; standard looks like 'normal' but means a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Ensign is the flag flown by British merchant ships, and a standard is a flag.
